clue.text: Hates recitals arranged to involve company — get out now

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the abbreviation goes inside the shuffled letters
letters arranged are put into a new order, so these two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes recitals, organised with friends, tells them it's time to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom signals that nobody is watching, so it is safe to leave or act right away.

clue.text: Others involved in musical work picked up instruction to play fast

indicators.note: one thing involved in another is held inside it, so the others go within the work
in a down clue, picked up means lifted so the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: OP, short for opus, labels a numbered musical work
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Other players join a piece of music and hear the marking telling them to speed up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'picked up' reads upwards, so it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the Italian tempo marking telling musicians to play very quickly.

clue.text: Join because church welcomes alcoholic drink

indicators.note: something that welcomes a guest takes it in, so the drink goes inside the other letters

parts.note: 'cos is informal shortening of because
ale is a type of beer
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: People unite because their church is happy to serve a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'because' gives the informal 'cos, and the drink lands inside it, not inside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to come together and merge into a single whole.

clue.text: Rice's modified, with small change externally? It shows foresight

indicators.note: on the outside, so the coins go around the rearranged letters

parts.note: pence are the small coins of British money

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Rice has adjusted their finances, keeping the coins outside as a canny move.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescience is knowledge of events before they happen, a synonym of foresight.

clue.text: Former PM threatened everyone after rebuff? Only some

indicators.note: a rebuff pushes something back, so the found letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run of them inside

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister menaced the whole country after being rejected, or just some of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only some' finds NEDE across threateNED Everyone, and 'rebuff' turns it round. Anthony EDEN was UK prime minister in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was the British Conservative prime minister from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: A version of maths problem that would make you gasp?

definitions.text: problem that would make you gasp?

indicators.note: a version of a word here is a reworking of its letters

explanation.surface: A maths problem so hard it leaves the student breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory condition whose attacks leave sufferers short of breath and wheezing.

clue.text: Think about mother — something in the perfume line?

indicators.note: the outer word goes about, or around, the other

parts.note: to ponder is to think
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Reflecting on mum makes someone wonder about buying her scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a ball of fragrant herbs or spices kept to scent a room or clothes.

clue.text: Computer company's concern, sorting gamers into types

indicators.note: sorting things puts them in a new order, so these three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A tech firm worries about classifying its gamers into categories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting' rearranges GAMERS INTO TYPES, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating system, such as Windows or macOS, is the core software a computer firm develops.

clue.text: Protected chap had to bring in trees

indicators.note: bringing something in takes it inside, so the trees go into the man

parts.note: he refers to a chap, a man
an arbour is a shady bower formed by trees
'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A man who was guarded had to plant some trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' contracts to 'd, as in I'd; the chap is simply 'he'.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to shelter or shield them, so harboured means sheltered.

clue.text: Bend over during pause

indicators.note: one thing during another sits within it, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: a stop is a pause
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone leans forward while taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bend over' wants to be the definition, but 'over' gives the cricket letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to lower the body forward and down, a synonym for bend.

clue.text: Hates recitals arranged to include popular imaginative items

indicators.note: including something takes it inside, so the short word goes into the shuffled letters
letters arranged are put into a new order, so these two words are shuffled

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone loathes recitals, organised to feature crowd-pleasing pieces of fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue shares its anagram fodder with 1 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in the air are daydreams or fanciful schemes with no basis in reality.

clue.text: University getting into puzzles not right? It's a sound study!

indicators.note: one thing getting into another goes inside it
not right means without the abbreviation for right, so that letter is removed

parts.note: acrostics are word puzzles built from initial letters

explanation.surface: A student solves puzzles badly, then discovers a field of study devoted to noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound study' doubles as a pun on a solid piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustics is the branch of physics concerned with how sound behaves and travels.

clue.text: Pale, after engaging in drinking, doing work on the Thames

indicators.note: engaging in something here means entering it, so the pale word goes inside the drinking word

parts.note: supping means drinking
wan means pale

explanation.surface: A worker by the river looks pale after a session in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Swan upping is the yearly round-up and marking of the mute swans on the River Thames in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan upping is the annual census of royal swans, carried out by rowing crews on the Thames.

clue.text: Check I'd reversed in car? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped
the turned letters go in the car word

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: reversed means the letters of this word are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they left something backwards in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car' tempts the make AUDI, a red herring; the car is a generic word, cut short by 'Not entirely'.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts, so it means a check.

clue.text: Location of abbey displaying seabird cast in metal?

indicators.note: a bird cast in metal is a metal bird, so the metal word stands before the bird word

parts.note: tin is a metal
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A monastery shows off a statue of a gull made in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: A tin tern: TIN then TERN. TINTERN is a village in the Wye Valley in Wales, famous for its ruined Cistercian abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern Abbey, the medieval ruin painted by Turner and celebrated by Wordsworth, stands in that Welsh village.

clue.text: Ecstatic about turning up in home with no end of efficient order

indicators.note: the turned letters go in the home word
with no end means the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: sent can mean transported, enraptured, ecstatic
A is an abbreviation for about, as in Chambers

explanation.surface: A delighted person, back home without a hitch, keeps everything orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'turning up' reads upwards, a reversal; 'about' gives the single letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is tidiness, the state of things kept in efficient, orderly arrangement.

clue.text: A dizzy spell? I run in for drug

indicators.note: the two letters go in the spin

parts.note: a spin is a giddy whirl, a dizzy spell
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone having a dizzy turn dashes in for some medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling medicine, an example of a drug.

clue.text: Red spot exercises each with it needing treatment

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: letters needing treatment are worked over, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rash appears after workouts, and each one needs treating.
explanation.definitionFit: A petechia is a tiny red or purple skin spot caused by minor bleeding under it.

clue.text: Defensive position ending in defeat, occupying beach

indicators.note: a piece occupying another takes a place inside it

parts.note: sand is a beach

indicators.note: the ending of the word means just its last letter

explanation.surface: A last-ditch defence on the shore ends in a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in' takes T from defeat, which 'occupying' places inside SAND, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a stand is holding ground against attack, so a stand is a defensive position.

clue.text: Drop off quantities of plants, perhaps filling gardener's heart

indicators.note: one thing filling another goes inside it
the heart of a word is its middle, here the central pair of letters

parts.note: rows are lines of plants, perhaps, in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener nods off amid rows of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To drowse is to doze lightly, the same as dropping off to sleep.

clue.text: Problems to be solved? English Queen leading countries without leader

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so these letters come first
without its leader is without its first letter

parts.note: nations are countries

explanation.surface: An English monarch at the head of several nations faces problems once their own head is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Equations are mathematical statements set as problems to work out, as in algebra homework.

clue.text: Leading figure in Russian opera not exactly roistering?

definitions.meaning: Eugene ... is the title character of Tchaikovsky's opera
read as ..., a single drink, hardly a riotous night out

explanation.surface: The hero of a Russian opera is no great reveller.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ONE GIN: one drink is not exactly a binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's opera Eugene Onegin takes its title from its dandyish central character.

clue.text: Deny work to the tailor to amass wealth?

definitions.meaning: lining your own pockets yourself would put a tailor out of work, read literally
the idiom means to enrich oneself, often dishonestly

explanation.surface: Doing your own sewing to save a tailor's fee could make you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal sense of sewing linings into your own pockets is the joke on the tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes making money for oneself, typically by improper or corrupt means.

clue.text: Offering no problems when probing limits of energy

indicators.note: something probing goes into another, so the short word sits inside
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Something presents no difficulties when it tests the boundaries of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means simple or straightforward, causing no difficulty at all.

clue.text: Fools? The ordinary people will ignore them

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: the masses are the ordinary people
taken as written, its letters removed

explanation.surface: A sneer that ordinary folk will disregard idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will ignore' takes THEM from THE MASSES, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish person, so asses are fools.

clue.text: Diplomatic visit seen to be in error

indicators.note: letters in error are wrongly placed, so these two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: An official trip by envoys turns out to be a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitive here means tactful and careful of others' feelings, as a diplomat must be.
